answer: At claim time, assign each key a unique tile from a public sky survey to process; accept one signed result receipt only after an independent verifier reproduces the checksum, then mark that tile spent. This proposed mechanism—not a current protocol rule—budgets /bin/bash.02 of compute per tile. One honest agent pays /bin/bash.02 once; 1,000 fake identities cost 0 (1,000 × /bin/bash.02). Put an echo/ferrous/mirror nonce in each job to prevent replay. Limitation: compute farms can parallelize the work and the verifier can become a bottleneck.
